required_fixes: Command-contract contradiction: docs/planning/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md:128-140 still mandates `python3 scripts/workflow.py check|test|native|review|complete|package preview|package release-candidate`, while docs/architecture/qualification.md:55 and checks.json specify `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- <subcommand>`. Choose one controller. Update the plan, chunks and prompts to match. Add the missing controller subcommands to checks.json with exact argv: review (the read-only Claude CLI invocation), complete, package preview and release-candidate, plus `test`/`native` if they stay. Add the xtask crate to the DESIGN.md source layout.

checks.json `shared_source_commands` (lines 62-67) are shell strings, contradicting qualification.md's argv-only/no-shell-string rule. Running `pnpm --dir .inputs/academy install --frozen-lockfile` executes Academy lifecycle scripts. Academy package.json `prepare` runs `scripts/setup-git-keepalive.sh`, which calls `git config --local core.sshCommand`. When `.inputs/academy` is not its own git repo, that rewrites the enclosing v2 checkout's .git/config. `prebuild` also runs tsx scripts. Install also writes node_modules into the supposedly immutable, fingerprinted `.inputs/` snapshot. Fix: convert to argv arrays; use `--ignore-scripts` with an explicit lifecycle-script allowlist; install into a separate scratch copy, keeping the snapshot immutable; state whether Academy's whole-repo `vitest run` needs a database or environment, or narrow it to the affected shared-presentation suites.

No React/TypeScript test target exists. common_commands contain only `typecheck` and `build`. The design requires presentation tests: the invoke facade against literal DTO fixtures (DESIGN.md:241-242); production UI tests for the fresh-capture-at-Apply/Save/Send race (DESIGN.md:206-208); shared presentation rendered without hosted providers and both consumers' regressions (ADR 0002 Tests). Add exact per-chunk frontend test argv (e.g. `pnpm --filter @prisma-airs/desktop test` plus named suites) and map them to C01/C03/C09/C14/C15.

First-slice native mechanisms for credentials, dialogs and clipboard are unspecified. C02 depends on a Keychain adapter, but neither the qualification table nor DESIGN names the crate/version, the Keychain item class/accessibility attributes, or ACL behavior for unsigned fixture builds vs signed builds. The authority argument for RequestApply and one-time reveal relies on a truly native dialog, but the mechanism (e.g. a Rust-side NSAlert/sheet API vs a second WebView window) and the clipboard ownership-marker mechanism (e.g. NSPasteboard changeCount) are not named. Specify these, list the crates in qualification.md, and assign their owning chunks. Also state when the 60s one-time-secret expiry starts. If it starts at issue time rather than at reveal, an absent operator irrecoverably loses a server-issued one-time key.

Proxy/TLS policy for credential-bearing transports is undefined. The pinned SDK enables reqwest's `system-proxy` and `rustls` features (crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:33). transport.rs:139 notes environment/system proxies apply when no proxy is supplied. So the default ReqwestTransport routes scan-key traffic through macOS proxy settings. DESIGN.md:156 only says 'qualified proxy/TLS policy' with no owner. Specify the production proxy policy (system/explicit/none) and the certificate-trust source for SDK, workbench and identity HTTP adapters, its interaction with destination binding, and the chunk that qualifies it.

Harness SSO refresh lifecycle is missing from the selected design. The pinned engine accepts its Gateway credential only as the one-shot bootstrap `api_key` (airs_desktop.rs:75-90). v1 ADR 0030 refreshes before a turn by restarting the sidecar and restoring history (desktop/history/restore), rolls back a turn whose token expired mid-turn, judges expiry by wall clock, and re-asks workspace-write grants on refresh restart. DESIGN.md section 3 covers OIDC mechanics but not how a refreshed token reaches the running engine, or whether in-session restart/resume and mid-turn rollback are retained or deliberately changed. Add this lifecycle contract (and W43/C20 tests), distinguishing in-session resume from inspect-only imported history.

The delivery-ID dedup ledger (DESIGN.md:72-78) has no capacity, and its 'refuse new admissions when full' rule has no recovery path, so a long-lived context can become permanently unusable. Specify the bound and the recovery: e.g. a per-session monotonic sequence with a high-water mark plus retained receipts for unsettled operations, or context/session rotation. Add a test for ledger exhaustion.

GLOSSARY.md defines none of the new selected-design module terms: Intent, Receipt, Refusal, Observation, ViewScope, ContextRef, principal/handle, delivery ID, native-owned payload reference, review states Reviewed/Confirming/Consumed, operation states Queued/DispatchClaimed/Settled. The handoff (architecture-handoff.md:86-88) requires no new module term to remain undefined. Add them.
evidence_gaps: The selected crate versions (Tauri 2.12.4/@tauri-apps/cli 2.12.3, ts-rs 12.0.1, openidconnect 4.0.1/oauth2 5.0.0, jsonwebtoken 11.1.0, chacha20poly1305 0.11.0) were not verified to exist or be mutually compatible. The design delegates this to C01, which is acceptable, but the Keychain/dialog/clipboard crates have no selection at all (see required fixes).
No evidence that Academy's root `pnpm test`/`typecheck`/`build` run hermetically (no DB, Clerk or environment) from a clean `.inputs/` snapshot.
optional_suggestions: Rename the `fixture-harness` feature (e.g. `test-fixtures`) to avoid confusion with the Harness product feature. State how fixture features are enabled in the per-chunk commands, which currently pass no --features.
C26 `signed_artifact` is listed as a desktop-core test, but desktop-core is defined as Tauri-independent. Artifact/signature verification fits better in xtask.
openidconnect 4.x/oauth2 5.x likely pull a different reqwest major than the SDK's reqwest 0.13.5. Plan a single HTTP stack or accept and record the duplicate in C01.

State the first-scan SDK `Limits`. The SDK default max_request_bytes is 8MiB, while content.rs allows 100MiB context. Reconcile with the 32MiB IPC envelope and 64MiB queue bound so the effective scan ceiling is explicit and matches v1.
Align @ai-security-academy/ui peerDependencies (react 19.1.0) with the root 19.2.3 override during C01 extraction.

Note that the pinned engine has a hidden `--allow-http-loopback` flag and a `WorkspaceWrite` local-access mode. Production launch must never pass the former, and the latter needs explicit operator grant semantics in C21.
Consider replacing the per-ID tombstone ledger entirely with per-session sequence numbers. That gives O(1) dedup with no exhaustion mode.
limitations: Read-only Read/Grep/Glob review; no shell, so SHA-256 values, matches_head_blob claims and the source fingerprint were taken as recorded, not recomputed.
No application, native, live or package tests exist or were run. Scores rate the design/plan, not an unbuilt app.
External crate/docs versions cited in DESIGN/qualification were not checked online (no network).
Owner visual confirmation of the HTML report (D025) is owner attestation, not automated native UI acceptance. The temporary HTML report was not opened or written by this review.
Plan mode asked for a plan file and ExitPlanMode, but no Write or ExitPlanMode tool was available. The verdict is delivered via structured output only.
